headline: Approved the Office of Youth Services reorganization and Manchester School District agreement, plus several staffing changes in city departments.
summary: The committee approved staffing changes in several city departments, including Water Works, Police, and Information Systems. It also unanimously approved a reorganization of the Office of Youth Services, which includes a memorandum of understanding with the Manchester School District that the School District must still sign off on.
decisions: Approved changing one full-time HR Generalist position to 32 hours per week part-time and eliminating one vacant Administrative Assistant II position.
Approved adding one full-time Accountant I position and eliminating one full-time Inventory Specialist I position in Central Fleet Management.
Approved eliminating three Accounting Technician II positions, adding one Accountant I position, and adding two Customer Service Representative III positions in Water Works.
Approved creating one full-time Administrative Compliance Coordinator, grade 124, in the Police Department, and leaving the Grants Coordinator and Accreditation Coordinator positions vacant.
Approved removing two Computer Systems Specialist II positions, grade 114, from the Police Department and adding them to the Information Systems Department.
Approved adding one full-time Police Financial Administrator, grade 121, and eliminating one full-time Business Services Manager, grade 120, in the Police Department.
Approved adding one full-time Police Lieutenant position, grade 126, to oversee the Parking Unit.
Approved adding one full-time Business Services Manager, grade 120, and eliminating one full-time Office Administrator I, grade 111, in Information Systems.
Approved unanimously the reorganization of the Office of Youth Services, including a Memorandum of Understanding with the Manchester School District.

transcript:
## COMMITTEE ON HUMAN RESOURCES/INSURANCE

October 6, 2026 Immediately Following Bills on Second Reading

Chairman Goonan called the meeting to order.

The Clerk called the roll.

Present: Aldermen Goonan, Sapienza, O’Neil, Burkush, Vincent

Messrs.: Mayor Ruais, J. Corwin, P. Croasdale, K. Loui, E. Rice

1. Communication from Jaime Corwin, Human Resources Director, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

• Modification of one (1) full-time HR Generalist position, grade 107, to 32 hours per week part-time, grade 112;

• Eliminate one (1) vacant Administrative Assistant II position, grade 105

Alderman Sapienza: I have a quick question. So if I'm reading this right, we're downsizing here. Is that right?

Jamie Corwin, Human Resources Director: I currently have a part time Administrative Assistant II who works 32 hours a week, and they've taken on all of the duties related to the HR Generalist that became vacant with a payroll change and with Karen Poulin leaving the HR Department back in May. So my Administrative Assistant has taken on greater responsibilities, but she only works 32 hours a week. And that's all that we need at this point. I'd like to take my vacant HR Generalist, adjust the scope of work to be what it's actually doing with the appropriate grade, and reduce it from full time to part time, and then move her into that and eliminate her administrative assistant role.

Alderman O'Neil: You still have an Assistant Director position that was budgeted for that will need to get filled at some point, right?

J. Corwin: Correct.

Alderman O’ Neil: Is it created or do you have to create it?

J. Corwin: I drafted the class spec for it; it's in a draft stage at this point, and then we'll be ready to roll it forward probably in the next few weeks.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to approve.

2. Communication from Chris Goodnow, Central Fleet Management Director, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

- • Add one (1) full-time Accountant I position, grade 108
- • Eliminate one (1) full-time Inventory Specialist I position, grade 108

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman O’ Neil , it was voted to approve.

3. Communication from Phil Croasdale, Water Works Director, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

• Eliminate three (3) Accounting Technician II positions, grade 107;

• Add one (1) Accountant I position, grade 108;

• Add two (2) Customer Service Representative III positions, grade 108

Alderman Sapienza: What's the net here? Is this a push or a reduction or a plus?

Phil Croasdale, Water Works Director: Right now, the whole department's pretty much Customer Service Representative III. I'm just trying to homogenize the whole department and keep people from flipping around. The Accounting Technician II used to be a grade higher than the customer service rep with Yarger Decker. Now they're lower. I get people with accounting backgrounds going into taking jobs as a customer service rep to get a pay increase. So it creates a little bit of a disruption. So with this change, I'm going to have all customer service reps on the billing side, and all Accountant I positions in the general accounting area for entry level positions. So they'll be the same grade and there'll be no flip flopping.

Alderman Sapienza: This doesn't represent an increase in spending. It does not. It's a push. It just makes things easier for you.

Alderman O'Neil: Is Patty one of these?

P. Croasdale: She already made a move.

Alderman O'Neil: I didn't even know who this woman was until about two months ago. She was a rock star.

P. Croasdale: She was an Accounting Tech II. And then she took one of the customer service rep jobs to get a promotion.

Alderman O'Neil: She's outstanding in helping people out.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to expedite the committee’ s report to the full Board.

4. Communication from Peter Marr, Chief of Police, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

- • Creation and addition of one (1) full-time Administrative Compliance
- Coordinator, grade 124;

- • Leave the Grants Coordinator position, grade 117, and Accreditation
- Coordinator position, grade 116, vacant

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to approve.

5. Communication from Richard Martinez, Information Systems Director, and Ken Loui, Assistant Chief of Police, requesting the following changes to their departments' complements:

• Remove two (2) Computer Systems Specialist II positions, grade 114, from the Police Department;

• Add two (2) Computer Systems Specialist II positions, grade 114, to the Information Systems Department

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman O’ Neil , it was voted to approve.

6. Communication from the Assistant Chief of Police requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

• Add one (1) full-time Police Financial Administrator position, grade 121 • Eliminate one (1) full-time Business Services Manager, grade 120

Alderman Sapienza: Could you just briefly explain what the difference between the two is and what their roles are?

Ken Loui, Assistant Chief of Police: The differences are significant. That is why, included in the attachment, are the job descriptions for the current Business Services Manager position and the proposed Police Financial Administrator position, so that you can compare them side by side. It would take too long for me to go through all the differences. Suffice it to say that with the addition of the parking unit to the police department, that is a significant enterprise that generates a lot of revenue, which is now being managed by our current Business Services Manager. What she's being asked to do right now is far beyond the scope of a Business Services Manager and more in line with what a Financial Administrator would be asked to do. There is a counterpart at the Health Department. They have a Health Financial Administrator as well. So this is kind of like the police counterpart to the to the Health Financial Administrator.

Alderman Sapienza: This is kind of spurred by the addition of the parking position.

K. Loui: Yes, sir. There's significant responsibilities attached to that to include ensuring that financial audit trails exist.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to approve.

Alderman O’ Neil: Does that need to report tonight? I know you’ re trying to get the parking transition completed.

K. Loui: No, not this particular item.

7. Communication from the Assistant Chief of Police requesting the addition of one (1) full-time Police Lieutenant position, grade 126, to the department's

- complement to oversee the Parking Unit.

Alderman Sapienza: This is basically the same idea with the addition of the parking responsibilities. It's what kind of spurred this.

K. Loui: That is correct.

Mayor Ruais: This is, in effect, what we requested of you guys, that you would have two months to get your sea legs, and figure out what the needs were. Now this has come over to the department and now we can make decisions based off the data that you've gathered over that time period to determine what your needs are.

K. Loui: Yes, Your Honor, that is accurate.

Mayor Ruais: And to confirm our conversation earlier today, you guys are in a good position from a budget standpoint, but also it seems like with the addition of the PSOs that this is actually going to increase the revenue for that department for the balance of the year. Correct?

K. Loui: That's correct.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Sapienza , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to expedite the committee’ s report to the full Board.

8. Communication from the Information Systems Director requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

- • Add one (1) full-time Business Services Manager position, grade 120
- • Eliminate one (1) full-time Office Administrator I position, grade 111

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to approve.

9. Communication from Mayor Ruais requesting approval of a reorganization of the Office of Youth Services, including entering into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Manchester School District.

Alderman Vincent moved to approve. Alderman O’ Neil duly seconded the motion.

Alderman O'Neil: Your Honor, we're going to achieve getting OYS workers out in the field and out of offices?

Mayor Ruais: Yes, so part of the conversation that we had in my office last week, what we really tried to do here was strike that balance and blend from what we heard from the community, from the Board of Aldermen, from the school district, from the Health Department, and making sure that we were meeting the requests of all those entities. And we heard you loud and clear. This really just formalizes what we had talked about with regard to people still being out in the community, while they're also attending to the school and the kids that are in need. But yes, they will be out in the community and they have the flexibility to do that. As you can see in the proposed organizational chart, it's explicitly written out there that there's time spent in the field.

Alderman Sapienza: Any word from the state police on their criminal investigation?

Emily Rice, Solicitor: As far as I know, the investigation is ongoing. I did, in anticipation of tonight, reach out for an update, and I have not heard back yet.

Chairman Goonan called for a vote. The motion passed unanimously.

Alderman O’ Neil: Does this have to be reported tonight?

Mayor Ruais: No, sir. We'll follow the regular course of business. The memorandum of understanding that's included in here, we will be bringing that to the Board of School Committee next week because they have to sign off on the MOU. So, there's no urgency here.

Chairman Goonan: And this is a this is a pilot program, correct?

Mayor Ruais: Yes.

Chairman Goonan: They can make changes if needed?

Mayor Ruais: That's exactly right. The intent behind this, in the last five years, we've had two full directors and one interim director. And what I didn't want to do going forward is say, this is going to be the direction of the department without doing the last 6 or 7 months of work: meeting with our community groups, meeting with the aldermen, meeting with the school district, hearing from Director Thomas and the Health Department about the community needs assessment, etc. Alderman O'Neil has talked about that a number of times, with those four pillars. So the idea behind this is that were the Boards to approve this by the end of October, we would begin in January. You get six months of the school year, January to June. The MOU requires them to work with the school district throughout the summer as well on the Leadership Academy, Freshman Academy, get those kids transitioned at the high school level, and then an additional school year from September to June of 2028. And then after that 18 month period, we will have 18 months of data to determine if it did or did not work, and to see what worked well, and what didn't work. We will be able to determine what changes need to be made. And then we'll be making decisions off of data.

Alderman O'Neil: Thank you to the OYS staff for going out and knocking on doors two weeks before school started. They knocked on a whole lot of doors to try to address the attendance issue, I think successfully. I don't know if we have any data yet.

Mayor Ruais: I believe the number was 209 referrals through that door knocking process.

Alderman O'Neil: And we hope most of them showed up. And then, as she has done many times, Elaine Michaud, the outstanding work she did in pulling all this information together.

Mayor Ruais: I would extend that kudos because not only did she do the interview work with the entire staff of the Office of Youth Services over a 6 to 7 week period, she did the operational assessment and went around the city and talked to a whole host of different nonprofits that are working in this space with kids. She did the same thing with the school district. There is an 11 page operational assessment that was the culmination of months of work above and beyond her duties at the Health Department. So the work that you're seeing here today, this 92 page packet, is the result of the efforts that Elaine put in over the last several months. So huge thanks and kudos to her.

There being no further business, on motion of Alderman Sapienza , duly seconded by

Alderman Vincent , it was voted to adjourn.

A True Record. Attest.

Clerk of Committee
